description: One module carrying the whole Airwindows effect collection, 456 separate stereo effects in this build, one of which runs at a time on the stereo input

params.text: Sets one parameter of the chosen effect; the name printed against it, the reading in its tooltip and the span it covers all come from that effect and change when another effect is chosen
Scales the CV input on the same row from -1 to +1 before that CV is added to the parameter knob, and at 0 the CV makes no difference
Scales what both input jacks feed into the effect, 0 to 100 percent, where 100 percent puts a 5V signal into the effect at full scale
Scales what the effect sends to both output jacks, 0 to 100 percent, where 100 percent sends the effect's full scale out as 5V

inputs.text: L input — the left channel into the effect, and with nothing patched to the R input it feeds the right channel too
R input — the right channel into the effect, taken from the L input instead while nothing is patched here
Adds to the parameter knob on the same row after the small knob there scales it; 5V through a fully clockwise scale knob covers that parameter's travel, and the total is clamped to its ends

outputs.text: L output — the left channel out of the effect, at 5V for the effect's full scale
R output — the right channel out of the effect, at 5V for the effect's full scale

notes: the effect is not chosen with a knob. Click the effect name at the top of the panel, or the category above it, for a menu with a search field, a list per category and a collection filter.
the arrows step through the effects in category order and then alphabetically by name, wrapping from the last back to the first, and they ignore the Categories in 'Chris' Order setting.
the question mark at the top of the panel opens Chris Johnson's own text about the chosen effect as an overlay across the module; clicking it again closes it.
the number of parameter knobs follows the chosen effect, between none and ten, and the knobs for parameters that effect does not have are taken off the panel.
the effect works on blocks of samples rather than one sample at a time, four samples by default. A larger block set from the panel menu costs less processor time and delays the sound more.
a new module comes up on Galactic, a reverb, and the arrow on either side of the effect name steps to the next effect without opening a menu.
a CV input stays on the panel, drawn dimmed, when the chosen effect has no parameter on its row, and nothing in the module reads it.
menu: Panic Reset — builds the chosen effect again from scratch, clearing the delay lines and filter state it is holding, and leaves the knob settings alone
Monophonic (Sum Inputs) — runs one copy of the effect, adding all the channels at each input jack together into one signal
Monophonic (MixMaster Sum Input) — runs one copy of the effect, reading each input jack as MixMaster's interleaved left-right pairs and adding those pairs into one stereo signal
Polyphonic (Stereo to Stereo) — runs a separate copy of the effect on each channel of the input jacks, up to 16 of them, and puts each result on the matching channel of the output jacks
Polyphonic (MixMaster to MixMaster) — runs a separate copy of the effect on each interleaved left-right pair at the input jacks and writes the results back out as interleaved pairs
Polyphonic (MixMaster to Stereo) — reads interleaved left-right pairs at the input jacks and sends each pair's result out as its own channel of the L and R outputs
Polyphonic (Stereo to MixMaster) — reads each channel of the L and R inputs as one stereo pair and writes the results out interleaved
Block Size — a submenu offering 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 samples, the first marked 4 (Lowest Latency) and the last 64 (Less CPU); the size in force is printed in the submenu's own name
Lock Effect Choice — stops the effect being changed, greys out the arrows and disables every effect name in the menus
Randomize Changes FX Choice — makes Rack's randomize pick a new effect as well as new knob settings, and is overruled by Lock Effect Choice
Categories in Alphabetical Order — lists the effects inside each category menu by name
Categories in 'Chris' (quality) Order — lists the effects inside each category menu in the order Chris Johnson gives them in the Airwindopedia, which he arranges by quality rather than by name
Filter by Collection: Basic, Recommended, Latest, All Effects — on the menu that opens from the effect name: narrows the category lists, the search and the arrows to that collection
